factcheck.claim: Framer Basic plan is $10/mo billed yearly in October 2026, charged per site.
Webflow merged the former CMS ($23/mo) and Business ($39/mo) Site plans into a single Premium Site plan at $25/mo billed yearly with 20,000 CMS items in May 2026.
There is no automated migration path between Framer and Webflow — switching requires rebuilding the site.
Framer server-renders HTML so Googlebot and AI crawlers get full pages without executing JavaScript; roughly 63% of Framer sites pass all three Core Web Vitals.
Webflow sites pass Core Web Vitals at roughly 58%, well above the WordPress baseline of about 42%.

competition.evidence: Top-10 SERP is populated by small marketing-studio and affiliate blogs (veloxthemes, althunt, waidastudio, flowout, siter, frprotech, insidea, layer3labs, itsbuzzinteractive) rather than official docs, big media, or wikis — classic winnable long-tail profile for a new domain.

demand.evidence: Nine top-10 results explicitly target 'framer vs webflow' with 2026 freshness, and sibling tails 'framer vs webflow for a startup landing page' and 'framer vs webflow 2026' show live search demand throughout October 2026.

intent.evidence: Entire top 10 is blog/informational comparison posts with pricing tables and decision checklists — no official product pages, video-only results, or transactional pages. A long-form comparison blog post is exactly what the SERP rewards.

gaps.gap: Most top-10 posts quote Framer's '$10/mo Basic' sticker but never flag Framer's per-site billing rule, where 3+ landing pages = 3+ separate subscriptions — a key cost trap for agencies and multi-brand founders.
gaps.covered_in: 2026 pricing — the per-site trap most roundups miss

gaps.gap: Half of the 2026 comparisons still cite Webflow's retired CMS ($23) and Business ($39) plans without noting the May 2026 merge into Premium ($25) with 20,000 CMS items — leading readers to compare the wrong Webflow number.
gaps.covered_in: 2026 pricing — the per-site trap most roundups miss

gaps.gap: Top posts rarely price three concrete landing-page shapes (solo founder, 5-site agency, product company with a blog) side-by-side with real yearly totals — most jump straight to a feature table.
gaps.covered_in: Three real landing page shapes priced for 2026

gaps.gap: Few posts explicitly flag Framer's SEO limit that editable canonical URLs require the Enterprise plan — a real blocker for organic-first landing pages competing against established content sites.
gaps.covered_in: Where Webflow still wins for landing pages (be honest)

own_evidence.desc: Directly verified both platforms' live pricing on October 30, 2026 via WebFetch to the official pricing pages and cross-checked against three independent 2026 breakdowns.
own_evidence.proof: On the official Framer pricing page as of October 30, 2026, Basic is $10/mo billed yearly and Pro is $30/mo billed yearly

own_evidence.desc: Modeled three real landing-page shapes (solo founder, 5-site agency, product company with a blog) against both platforms' 2026 list prices with explicit yearly totals.
own_evidence.proof: Framer Basic × 5 sites: $50/mo = $600/yr, each site billed independently per the Siter and Goodspeed per-site rule. Webflow Basic × 5 site plans inside one Workspace: $75/mo = $900/yr in site plans.

own_evidence.desc: Built an original 10-row feature matrix comparing Framer and Webflow for a single marketing landing page, including rows (editable canonicals, 301 manager, native ecommerce) most competitors skip.
own_evidence.proof: Framer wins the top three rows that matter most for a single marketing page. Webflow wins the next three rows that matter if the landing page is really a chapter of a larger site.

own_evidence.desc: Compiled a side-by-side 2026 pricing comparison with Framer per-site billing explicitly separated from Webflow's Workspace model.
own_evidence.proof: Three landing pages on Framer Basic is $30/mo; three Webflow Basic sites inside one Workspace is $45/mo in site plans but may still be cheaper after seat and Workspace math
